'''Michael Edward Peskin''' (born October 27, 1951, [[Philadelphia]]) is an American [[theoretical physicist]].<ref name="Stoddart">{{cite journal |last1=Stoddart |first1=Charlotte |title=How particle accelerators came to be |journal=Knowable Magazine |date=29 March 2022 |doi=10.1146/knowable-032822-1|doi-access=free |url=https://knowablemagazine.org/article/physical-world/2022/how-particle-accelerators-came-be |access-date=24 May 2023 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  He is currently a professor in the [[SLAC Theory Group|theory group]] at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref name="Case">{{cite web |title=Michael Peskin – SM@50: The Standard Model At 50 Years |url=https://artsci.case.edu/smat50/michael-peskin/ |website=© 2023 Case Western Reserve University |access-date=24 May 2023}}</ref> 

Peskin has been recognized for his work in proposing and analyzing unifying models of elementary particles and forces in theoretical elementary particle physics, and proposing experimental methods for testing such models.<ref name="AAAS"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eichten |first1=Estia J. |last2=Lane |first2=Kenneth D. |last3=Peskin |first3=Michael E. |title=New Tests for Quark and Lepton Substructure |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=14 March 1983 |volume=50 |issue=11 |pages=811–814 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.811|bibcode=1983PhRvL..50..811E |osti=1446807 |s2cid=119918703 }}</ref> His textbook, ''[[An Introduction to Quantum Field Theory]]'' (1995), co-authored with Daniel Schroeder, is widely used in graduate physics courses. [[Peskin–Takeuchi parameter|Peskin–Takeuchi parameters]] are named after him.

==Education==
Michael Peskin is a fourth generation descendant of Jewish-Lithuanian emigrants from the [[Pale of Settlement]]. Both of his parents became medical doctors. Peskin attended [[Lower Merion High School]] in the [[Philadelphia Main Line|Philadelphia area]] and later [[New Trier High School|New Trier West]] in the Chicago suburbs.<ref name="AIP"/>

Peskin was an undergraduate at [[Harvard University]]. He obtained his Ph.D. in 1978 from [[Cornell University]] under the supervision of [[Kenneth G. Wilson|Kenneth Wilson]]. He was a junior fellow at the [[Harvard Society of Fellows]] from 1977–1980.<ref name="AIP">{{cite web |title=Interview of Michael Peskin by David Zierler on April 27, 2021 |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/47471 |website=Niels Bohr Library & Archives, American Institute of Physics |access-date=24 May 2023 |language=en |date=14 December 2022}}</ref>

== Career ==
After receiving his Ph.D. from Cornell University, Peskin served as a junior fellow of the [[Harvard Society of Fellows]] from 1977 to 1980.<ref>{{cite web |title=Listed by Term |url=https://socfell.fas.harvard.edu/listed-term-0 |website=Harvard Society of Fellows |language=en}}</ref> He also held postdoctoral appointments at [[CEA Paris-Saclay|Saclay Nuclear Research Centre]] (1979–1980) and Cornell (1980–1982).<ref>{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae Michael E. Peskin |url=https://cap.stanford.edu/profiles/viewCV?facultyId=86080&name=Michael_Peskin |website=Stanford University}}</ref><ref name="AIP"/>  In 1982, Peskin joined the faculty of the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory at [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Energy |first1=United States Department of |title=High Energy Physicists and Graduate Students: 1985 Census |date=1985 |publisher=DOE |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4qTvAAAAMAAJ&dq=1982%2C+Peskin+stanford&pg=PT349 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2000, Peskin was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Michael E. Peskin |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/michael-e-peskin |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en |date=27 July 2023}}</ref>  He was appointed a co-editor of the journal ''[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]'' as of 2023.<ref name="AR2023">{{cite journal |title=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/journal/nucl |website=Annual Reviews |access-date=24 May 2023}}</ref> He also serves on the Board of Directors of [[Annual Reviews (publisher)|Annual Reviews]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annual Reviews Board of Directors |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/about/our-team |website=Annual Reviews}}</ref>

==Research==
Peskin has worked on many aspects of quantum field theory and elementary particle physics, exploring and going beyond the [[Standard Model]] of particle physics to explore [[Technicolor (physics)|technicolor theories]].<ref name="beyond">{{cite book |last1=Peskin |first1=M. E. |title=Beyond the Standard Model |date=1 May 1997 |publisher=SLAC National Accelerator Lab., Menlo Park, CA (United States) |url=https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/515615 |language=English}}</ref> Peskin and Daniel V. Schroeder's widely used textbook on [[quantum field theory]], ''[[An Introduction to Quantum Field Theory]]'' (1995, 2018) is considered a classic in the field.<ref name="Berg"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Reviews: ''Quantum Field Theory and the Standard Model'' by Matthew D. Schwartz |url=https://schwartzqft.fas.harvard.edu/reviews |website= |language=en|publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="Lellouch">{{cite book |last1=Lellouch |first1=Laurent |title=Modern Perspectives in Lattice QCD: Quantum Field Theory and High Performance Computing: Lecture Notes of the Les Houches Summer School: Volume 93, August 2009 |date=August 25, 2011 |publisher=OUP Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-969160-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lTnLFQAfZ5QC&pg=PA15 |language=en}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=15}} More recently, he has written ''Concepts of Elementary Particle Physics'' (2019), a textbook on the Standard Model.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Peskin |first1=Michael Edward |title=Concepts of Elementary Particle Physics |date= |publisher=Oxford University Press |location= |isbn=978-0-19-881218-0|year=2009}}</ref>

In 1990, Peskin and Tatsu Takeuchi proposed the parameterization of a set of three measurable quantities, called ''S'', ''T'', and ''U'', that are used to describe and simplify precision
electroweak fits. These parameters are sensitive to new physics which contributes to oblique corrections.<ref name="Hewett">{{cite arXiv |last1=Hewett |first1=J. L. |title=The Standard Model and Why We Believe It |date=9 Oct 1998 |eprint=hep-ph/9810316 }}</ref><ref name="Wells">{{cite journal |last1=Wells |first1=James D. |last2=Zhang |first2=Zhengkang |title=Renormalization group evolution of the universal theories EFT |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |date=June 2016 |volume=2016 |issue=6 |article-number=122 |doi=10.1007/JHEP06(2016)122 |url= |arxiv=1512.03056 |bibcode=2016JHEP...06..122W |s2cid=256036070 }}</ref><ref name=PesTak>{{cite journal | author=Michael E. Peskin | author2=Tatsu Takeuchi | name-list-style=amp | title=New constraint on a strongly interacting Higgs sector | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=65 | date=1990 | issue=8 | pmid=10043071 | pages=964–967 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.65.964 | bibcode=1990PhRvL..65..964P}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=Michael E. Peskin | author2=Tatsu Takeuchi | name-list-style=amp | title=Estimation of oblique electroweak corrections | journal=[[Physical Review D]] | volume=46 | date=1992 | issue=1 | pages=381–409 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.46.381| pmid=10014770 |bibcode = 1992PhRvD..46..381P }}</ref> They are now called the [[Peskin–Takeuchi parameter]]s.<ref name="Carpenter">{{cite journal |last1=Carpenter |first1=Linda M. |last2=Murphy |first2=Taylor |last3=Smylie |first3=Matthew J. |title=Changing patterns in electroweak precision fits with new color-charged states: Oblique corrections and the W -boson mass |journal=Physical Review D |date=6 September 2022 |volume=106 |issue=5 |article-number=055005 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.106.055005|arxiv=2204.08546 |bibcode=2022PhRvD.106e5005C |s2cid=248239692 }}</ref>

Peskin uses high energy colliders to search for new physical interactions on the basis of high-precision observations and measurements of elementary particles, including the W and Z bosons, the top quark, and the Higgs boson.<ref name="Charitos">{{cite news |last1=Charitos |first1=Panos |title=An interview with Michael E. Peskin |url=https://ep-news.web.cern.ch/content/interview-michael-e-peskin |work=EP News |date=28 June 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Einhorn">{{cite book |last1=Einhorn |first1=M. B. |title=The Standard Model Higgs Boson: Selections and Comments |date=2 December 2012 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-444-59613-0 |pages=379–380 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XTwUtB6hD3YC&pg=PA379 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Charley |first1=Sarah |title=What's next for Higgs boson research? |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/july-2014/whats-next-for-higgs-boson-research |work=symmetry magazine |date=July 4, 2014 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Murayama"/> He is interested in modelling dark matter<ref name="Bahcall">{{cite journal |last1=Bahcall |first1=Neta A. |title=Dark matter universe |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=6 October 2015 |volume=112 |issue=40 |pages=12243–12245 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1516944112|pmid=26417091 |pmc=4603491 |bibcode=2015PNAS..11212243B |doi-access=free }}</ref> and is an advocate of building a future [[linear collider]],<ref name="Cartlidge">{{cite journal |last1=Cartlidge |first1=Edwin |title=Physicists shrink plans for next major collider |journal=Nature |date=9 November 2017 |doi=10.1038/nature.2017.22983 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature.2017.22983 |access-date=24 May 2023 |language=en |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Murayama">{{cite journal |last1=Murayama |first1=Hitoshi |last2=Peskin |first2=Michael E. |title=Physics Opportunities of e+e- Linear Colliders |journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science |date=December 1996 |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=533–608 |doi=10.1146/annurev.nucl.46.1.533 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/full/10.1146/annurev.nucl.46.1.533 |language=en |issn=0163-8998|arxiv=hep-ex/9606003 |bibcode=1996ARNPS..46..533M |s2cid=16466403 }}</ref> a "factory" for the [[Higgs boson]].<ref name="Stoddart"/>
